identity.title: The ALMA Band 9 receiver. Design, construction, characterization, and first light

paper_type_evidence.quote: We describe the design, construction, and characterization of the Band 9 heterodyne receivers (600–720 GHz) for the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

question.value: Design, construction, laboratory performance and on-sky first-light performance of the ALMA Band 9 (600–720 GHz) receivers

evidence.quote: On-sky characterization and tests of the performance of the Band 9 cartridges are presented using commissioning data.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00007.SV.
Frequency range | 602–720 GHz

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four spectral windows including 12CO 6-5; spectrum binned to 1.95 MHz (~0.8 km/s)

evidence.quote: The four spectral windows are binned to a resolution of 1.95 MHz ($\sim$0.8 km s$^{-1}$)
with ALMA in a Cycle 0 extended configuration
resulting in a resolution of $\approx$0 $''$22

time_on_source.value: 9.2 hours total for seven-point mosaic including calibration

evidence.quote: A total of 9.2 hours were spent on a seven-point mosaic and the necessary calibration
Science Verification of Band 9 was undertaken on April 16 and 17, 2012

what.value: Observation and calibration details of IRAS 16293-2422 SV data given in CASA guide

evidence.quote: More detailed information on the observations and calibration can be found in the CASA guide

unstated_but_needed: Imaging parameters (weighting, cell, clean masks) for IRAS 16293 cubes
Calibration procedure, CASA version and calibrators for SV data

analysis_steps.goal: Extract Band 9 spectrum toward IRAS 16293 B

method.value: Spectrum averaged over a 0.3"x0.3" region centered on source B, binned to 1.95 MHz

evidence.quote: the spectrum is averaged over a $0\,\ensuremath{''}3\times0\,\ensuremath{''}3$ region centered on source B

used_for.value: Water vapor radiometer corrections applied to quasar test data

evidence.quote: Corrections using the water vapor radiometer solutions, derived using the WVRGCAL software (cite: Nikolic12), were applied in the test

used_for.value: Referenced via CASA guide for SV data reduction

evidence.quote: More detailed information on the observations and calibration can be found in the CASA guide

results_numeric.quantity: Average aperture efficiency of Band 9 receivers (62 cartridges)

evidence.quote: All phases are extremely flat with RMS numbers of $\sim$30–35 degrees.

results_numeric.quantity: Number of emission lines in IRAS 16293 B spectrum

evidence.quote: Over 100 emission lines are clearly visible in the spectrum.

findings_qualitative.value: All Band 9 receivers comply with ALMA specifications in the laboratory; AlN-barrier junctions cover the band better than AlOx

evidence.quote: The laboratory results show that all receivers complied with ALMA specifications prior to integration in the ALMA antennas.

claims.hypothesis: Do the Band 9 receivers meet ALMA specifications?
claims.experiment: Laboratory measurements of noise temperature, gain compression and beam on 73 cartridges
claims.result: All receivers perform better than the specification with margin; gain compression within 4%

evidence.quote: demonstrating that all the receivers perform better than the ALMA specifications (cf. Table [1](#table:specs)) with margin.

claims.hypothesis: Is Band 9 phase and amplitude stability good on sky?
claims.experiment: Quasar tracking and four-quasar phase-transfer tests
claims.result: Phase RMS 10–25 deg in four-quasar test; stable phases on J1924-292

evidence.quote: It can be concluded that the Band 9 performance is excellent in these on-sky tests.

limitations_admitted.value: CO 6-5 line profile not correctly cleaned and filtered by lack of short baselines

evidence.quote: CO $J$=6–5 emission extends over a large area (cite: 2013A&A...549L...6K), and is thus not correctly cleaned.

referee_caveats_inferred: On-sky tests are qualitative, with uncalibrated amplitudes and few baselines
ALMA science data processing not described

evidence.quote: This dataset is publicly available.

missing_for_reproduction: Full data reduction script (only via external CASA guide)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: tens of GB for the IRAS 16293 SV dataset
reproducibility.score_reason: Mostly hardware paper; ALMA data analysis is minimal and not detailed.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are hardware characterizations, not reproducible from ALMA data.
